newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Nestle unit pushes Philippines coffee development.
newsitem.headline: Nestle unit pushes Philippines coffee development.

text.p: The Philippines unit of Swiss food giant Nestle is pushing for a change in coffee cropping techniques in the country and is providing technical assistance to boost low yields, an official said on Wednesday.

Nestle Philippines Inc (NPI) vice-president John Pater told an Asia Coffee meeting in Vietnam that the Philippines 1995/96 coffee crop will reach an estimated 53,000 tonnes over an area of about 125,000 hectares.
The average yield reaches around 424 kgs a hectare.
"The major cause for the low yields in the Philippines is the lack of proper field management," he said.
The local Nestle unit buys about 75 percent of the green coffee produced in the Philippines.
Pater said NPI is providing technical assistance to coffee farmers in the Philippines and urging them to organise themselves in cooperatives.
NPI wants to remove the present system of permanent intercrops so as to encourage a change in favour of "more intensive coffee production" in the Philippines.
"NPI established 12 regional buying stations, enabling the coffee suppliers to deliver directly to NPI," Pater said.
